executiveSummary: Surveillance data spanning October 2025 through May 2026 from ECDC and PAHO reveal multiple concurrent biological threats across the Americas and Europe. Key concerns include ongoing Avian Influenza A(H5N1) activity in the Americas with persistent zoonotic spillover risk, a resurging dengue burden alongside chikungunya co-circulation, and the start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season overlapping with RSV activity. Measles re-emergence and escalating pertussis case counts reflect vaccination coverage gaps in the Americas region.
bottomLine: The Americas face a complex multi-pathogen threat landscape dominated by H5N1 spillover risk, record-level dengue transmission, and vaccine-preventable disease resurgence, while Europe continues routine communicable disease threat monitoring through weekly ECDC reporting cycles.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained H5N1 activity
Zoonotic spillover events documented in the Americas with human exposure risk from infected poultry and dairy herds
Dual animal and human surveillance alerts indicating widening geographic spread across the region
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance at human-animal interfaces; pre-position antiviral stockpiles; strengthen agricultural worker monitoring and PPE protocols

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued February 2026 signaling elevated case counts
Historically high transmission levels in multiple countries consistent with hyperendemicity
Co-circulation of multiple serotypes increases severe dengue and reinfection risk
threats.action: Scale up vector control operations; strengthen severe dengue case management capacity; activate cross-border data sharing among endemic countries

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza / Respiratory Virus Co-circulation
threats.pathogen: Influenza A and B viruses; Respiratory Syncytial Virus
signals: PAHO alert on simultaneous influenza and RSV circulation issued January 2026
Southern Hemisphere 2026 season onset confirmed by PAHO alert April 2026
Northern Hemisphere 2025-26 season start documented December 2025 creating year-round surveillance burden
threats.action: Promote seasonal influenza vaccination uptake in both hemispheres; enhance ICU surge capacity planning; monitor for novel reassortant strains

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 indicating ongoing transmission
Sustained community transmission signal requiring continued monitoring
Risk of clade differentiation and potential for increased severity
threats.action: Maintain ring vaccination strategies; reinforce clinical recognition and laboratory confirmation capacity; ensure contact tracing infrastructure remains active

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two consecutive PAHO epidemiological updates issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating rising case counts
Resurgence pattern consistent with waning vaccine immunity and coverage gaps
Infant and unvaccinated populations at highest risk for severe outcomes
threats.action: Audit and strengthen childhood immunization coverage; promote Tdap booster in pregnant women and close infant contacts; investigate potential macrolide resistance clusters

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating measles activity in the region
Risk of importation and outbreak in under-vaccinated communities
Americas region had achieved elimination status making any transmission a significant setback
threats.action: Conduct rapid coverage assessments; implement supplemental immunization activities in low-coverage areas; strengthen port-of-entry surveillance

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating chikungunya activity
Geographic overlap with dengue vectors increases dual infection risk
Alert timing suggests early-season amplification coinciding with arboviral transmission period
threats.action: Integrate chikungunya into existing arboviral surveillance platforms; ensure clinical differentiation from dengue; maintain vector control in affected areas

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
threats.pathogen: Sin Nombre virus / Andes virus (Hantavirus spp.)
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued December 2025 indicating HPS cases in the Americas
Rodent reservoir activity linked to environmental and seasonal conditions
High case fatality rate makes even small cluster events a significant public health concern
threats.action: Strengthen rodent exposure risk communication; enhance clinician awareness for early HPS recognition; ensure ribavirin access and ICU capacity at affected sites

amrSignals: Pertussis resurgence with two successive PAHO alerts raises concern for possible macrolide-resistant Bordetella pertussis strains warranting genotypic surveillance
Sustained bacterial pathogen circulation in the context of reduced healthcare access may promote empiric antibiotic misuse contributing to broader AMR selection pressure in the Americas
emergingPatterns: Temporal clustering of multiple PAHO alerts in early 2026 (January-April) suggests a broad seasonal surge period with simultaneous multi-pathogen pressure on health systems
Dual H5N1 alerts (November 2025 and March 2026) indicate sustained rather than transient zoonotic activity, raising pandemic preparedness concern
Co-circulation of dengue and chikungunya during the same arboviral season creates diagnostic confusion risk and may mask true burden of each pathogen
Vaccine-preventable disease resurgence (measles, pertussis) concurrent with arboviral and respiratory threats signals compounding immunity gaps in the Americas
Weekly ECDC reporting cadence through five consecutive weeks (Weeks 16-20, April-May 2026) without specific outbreak designations suggests European situation is managed but under active watch
